hello.note: Time-of-day greetings like selamat pagi are just as common. Many Muslims greet with assalamualaikum.

goodbye.note: Casual: dah! Selamat jalan is said to someone setting off on a trip.

please.note: Tolong asks for help or a favour. When offering (please, go ahead / help yourself), say silakan.

thank_you.note: Very grateful: terima kasih banyak. Casual: makasih.

yes.note: Iya is softer and very common in speech.

no.note: Casual: nggak. Bukan negates nouns instead: bukan yang ini (not this one).

sorry.note: Fuller apology: saya minta maaf. Formal: mohon maaf.

excuse_me.note: Also said when passing in front of someone. Adding Pak (to a man) or Bu (to a woman) is even politer.

good_morning.note: Until about 11 a.m. Then selamat siang (midday) and selamat sore (afternoon).

how_are_you.note: Warmer with a title: apa kabar, Pak? (to a man) / apa kabar, Bu? (to a woman).

im_fine.note: Also: kabar baik. To ask back: bagaimana dengan Anda?

whats_your_name.note: Anda is polite but formal; people often say Bapak (sir) or Ibu (madam) instead. Casual: namanya siapa?

my_name_is.note: Saya is the polite 'I'; with friends, aku.

nice_to_meet_you.note: Casual: salam kenal. Also: senang bertemu dengan Anda.

where_from.note: In speech also: asalnya dari mana?

speak_english.note: In speech often just: bisa bahasa Inggris?

dont_understand.note: Also: saya tidak paham. Casual: nggak ngerti.

speak_slowly.note: Softer, as a question: bisa bicara lebih pelan?

where.note: Where to: ke mana? Where from: dari mana?

what.note: To ask someone to repeat, maaf? or bagaimana? is politer than a bare apa?

when.note: Only for questions; in statements 'when' is ketika or waktu.

how_much.note: Pointing at something, simply: ini berapa?

where_bathroom.note: Also: kamar kecil (more polite) or WC, said weh-seh.

can_you_help.note: Also very natural: boleh minta tolong? (may I ask a favour?)

what_time.note: Also: sekarang jam berapa? Formal: pukul berapa sekarang?

what_means.note: About a word: apa arti kata ini?

one.note: In compounds it becomes se-: sepuluh (10), seratus (100), seribu (1,000).

four.note: The e is a short 'uh' sound, as in about. Same in enam, delapan and sembilan.

seven.note: The final h is lightly breathed, not silent.

ten.note: Literally 'one ten'. 11 is sebelas, 20 is dua puluh.

water.note: Plain drinking water (literally 'white water'). Air, said a-ir, alone is water in general.

tea.note: Usually served sweet; for unsweetened ask for teh tawar. Iced tea: es teh.

menu_please.note: To call staff: Mas! (to a young man) or Mbak! (to a young woman).

bill_please.note: Also common: minta bill-nya, or just ask the total: totalnya berapa?

no_meat.note: Daging often means red meat only; to be clear add: ayam dan ikan juga tidak (no chicken or fish either).

left.note: Calling kiri! is also how you ask a minibus (angkot) driver to stop.

stop_here.note: To a woman driver, end with Bu. Very common too: di sini saja, Pak (right here is fine).

hotel.note: Same word as in English. Cheaper guesthouses: penginapan or losmen.

train_station.note: Stasiun alone usually means the train station; a bus station is a terminal.

want_to_go.note: More formal: saya ingin pergi ke …

is_it_far.note: Casual: jauh nggak? More formal: apakah jauh dari sini?

one_ticket.note: Ending with ya softens a request, like please. Fuller: saya mau beli satu tiket.

too_expensive.note: Casual: mahal banget! To bargain: bisa kurang? (can you go lower?)

id_like_this.note: Also: saya ambil yang ini (I'll take this one).

just_looking.note: Also: lihat-lihat dulu, ya (just looking for now).

pay_card.note: More formal: bisa bayar dengan kartu? Credit card: kartu kredit; debit card: kartu debit.

cash.note: Also: uang tunai. In speech many simply say cash.

later.note: Vague on purpose: it can mean in a minute or in a few days.

good_evening.note: From about 6 p.m. Late afternoon: selamat sore.

good_night.note: Only before sleep. When leaving at night, people say selamat malam, the same as good evening.

see_you_later.note: Also: sampai ketemu lagi (see you again).

wait_moment.note: Very common: sebentar, ya! Formal: mohon tunggu sebentar.

help.note: The same tolong that makes a request polite.

dont_feel_well.note: Also: saya tidak enak badan. Saya sakit means I'm ill.

pharmacy.note: Small shops with basic medicines: toko obat.

hospital.note: Often shortened to RS on signs.

lost_phone.note: HP (said ha-peh) is the everyday word for a mobile phone; formal: ponsel.

be_careful.note: Also a friendly goodbye to someone setting off: hati-hati di jalan.

no_problem.note: Casual: nggak apa-apa (often said gapapa). Also: tidak masalah.

dont_know.note: Casual: nggak tahu, often said nggak tau.

i_like_it.note: Pointing at something: saya suka yang ini.

im_happy.note: Bahagia is a deeper, lasting happiness: saya bahagia.

welcome.note: Inviting a guest in: silakan masuk.

congratulations.note: The same selamat that starts greetings like selamat pagi.

mother.note: Also the polite way to address a woman (Bu). At home many children say mama.

father.note: Also: bapak, which shortens to Pak when addressing a man. At home many children say papa.

brother.note: In speech people say whether he is older or younger: kakak laki-laki / adik laki-laki.

sister.note: In speech people say whether she is older or younger: kakak perempuan / adik perempuan.

child.note: Son: anak laki-laki. Daughter: anak perempuan.

friend.note: The same word for a male or female friend. Casual: temen.

this_is_my_friend.note: The same for a female friend. Casual: ini temanku.

are_you_married.note: Asked with sudah (already). Instead of a flat no, people answer belum (not yet).

have_children.note: Also asked with sudah, and answered belum if not yet. Casual: udah punya anak?

sunday.note: Also means week, as in minggu depan (next week). Some people say Ahad.

weekend.note: In speech many just say weekend. Saturday night out is malam Minggu.

what_day.note: For the date: hari ini tanggal berapa?

next_week.note: More formal: pekan depan. Last week: minggu lalu.

eleven.note: 11 to 19 use belas: sebelas, dua belas, tiga belas and so on.

twenty.note: Tens use puluh: tiga puluh (30). 21 is dua puluh satu.

hundred.note: Se- means one. 200 is dua ratus.

thousand.note: 2,000 is dua ribu. Prices in rupiah are usually in thousands: lima puluh ribu (50,000).

how_old.note: More formal: berapa usia Anda? Casual: umurnya berapa?

years_old.note: Also: saya berumur … tahun. More formal: usia saya … tahun.

white.note: As in air putih, plain drinking water.

what_colour.note: Also: apa warnanya? Colours come after the noun: baju merah (a red shirt).

this_one.note: Yang makes 'the one': yang merah (the red one).

that_one.note: Further off: yang di sana (the one over there).

another_one.note: Lagi means more. Politer: boleh minta satu lagi?

its_hot.note: In speech people just exclaim: panas banget! (so hot!)

its_cold.note: Casual: dingin banget! In the mountains people often say udaranya dingin (the air is cold).

its_raining.note: Casual: lagi hujan. Heavy rain: hujan deras.

its_sunny.note: Cerah means clear and bright. Blazing sun: panas terik.

its_windy.note: Literally 'the wind is strong'. Also: banyak angin.

beautiful_day.note: Casual: cuacanya bagus banget! Hari yang indah sounds more poetic.

summer.note: Indonesia itself has a dry season (musim kemarau) and a rainy season (musim hujan).

have_reservation.note: Then give the name: atas nama … (in the name of …). Also: saya sudah reservasi.

room.note: Kamar mandi is a bathroom; kamar tidur, a bedroom.

luggage.note: Mainly checked luggage at the airport. A suitcase is koper; your things in general: barang.

wifi_password.note: Politer: boleh minta password Wi-Fi-nya? Formal signs say kata sandi.

check_out_time.note: Also: jam berapa harus check-out? (what time do I have to check out?)

bus.note: Said with an oo sound, like boos. Also written bis.

is_this_seat_free.note: Also very natural: ada orangnya? (is someone sitting here?)

what_do_you_do.note: People often ask instead: kerja di mana? (where do you work?)

i_work_in.note: Casual: saya kerja di … For example: di bank, or di bidang penjualan (in sales).

im_student.note: University student. A woman may say: saya mahasiswi. A school pupil: saya pelajar.

meeting.note: In many offices people just say meeting.

im_busy.note: Casual: lagi sibuk. Saya sibuk means busy in general.

day_off.note: Taking leave from work is cuti: saya sedang cuti (I'm on leave).

colleague.note: The same for a woman. In speech also: teman kantor (office friend).

lets_start.note: Also common: ayo kita mulai. Casual: yuk, mulai!

good_job.note: Also: hebat! or bagus sekali! Casual: mantap!

table_for_two.note: Staff often ask: berapa orang? (how many people?). Then just answer: dua orang.

what_recommend.note: For the house speciality: menu andalannya apa? Also: ada rekomendasi?

not_spicy.note: No chilli at all: tanpa cabai. Just a little spicy: sedikit pedas.

vegetarian_food.note: To ask: ada makanan vegetarian? Watch for terasi (shrimp paste) in sauces.

more_water.note: Minta (I'd like) is the everyday polite way to ask for things. With ice: pakai es.

no_sugar.note: Casual: nggak pakai gula. Less sugar: gulanya sedikit saja.

im_full.note: Casual: udah kenyang. Very full: kenyang sekali.

takeaway.note: Bungkus means wrap. Eating in: makan di sini.

it_was_delicious.note: Praising the cooking: masakannya enak sekali!

keep_change.note: Warmer: kembaliannya buat Mas saja (to a man) / buat Mbak saja (to a woman).

stomach.note: Also belly. Stomach ache: sakit perut.

head_hurts.note: Also: saya sakit kepala. Many say saya pusing, which covers headache and dizziness.

have_fever.note: Also: badan saya panas (my body is hot).

medicine.note: Add the problem: obat batuk (cough medicine), obat sakit kepala (headache medicine).

call_ambulance.note: More urgent and polite: tolong panggil ambulans!

need_rest.note: Also: saya butuh istirahat. Casual: aku mau istirahat dulu.

feel_better.note: In speech very common: sudah mendingan or sudah baikan.

lets_meet.note: Ketemuan is casual for meeting up. Friendlier: yuk, ketemuan! Formal: mari kita bertemu.

are_you_free.note: Casual: besok kosong? or besok sibuk nggak?

call_me.note: Also: hubungi saya (contact me). Many simply say WA saya, ya (WhatsApp me).

your_number.note: Everyday: boleh minta nomor HP-nya? Many people mean their WhatsApp number (nomor WA).

see_you_soon.note: Casual: sampai ketemu lagi! With a set day: sampai ketemu besok.

have_nice_day.note: Roughly 'enjoy your day's activities', like selamat bekerja. Also: semoga harinya menyenangkan!

good_luck.note: Also: semoga sukses! Before an exam or trip: semoga lancar!

happy_birthday.note: In messages often shortened: selamat ultah!

thanks_a_lot.note: Casual: makasih banyak! For help received: terima kasih atas bantuannya.

miss_you.note: Kangen is everyday; rindu is more poetic: aku rindu kamu. In messages just: kangen!
